title: Grand Duchy of Kraków
capsule: The medieval Grand Duchy (High Duchy) of Kraków designated the senior principality among the fragmented Polish Piast duchies, conferring the title of High Duke (princeps) on whichever Piast ruled Kraków. From 1279, following the death of Bolesław the Chaste, Leszek II the Black of Kujawy held the title; he repelled a Galician invasion at Goźlice in 1280 and survived the Mongol raid of 1287–1288, dying in Kraków on 30 September 1288. Henry Probus and then Przemysł II succeeded to the Kraków seat, which Władysław I Łokietek eventually unified with other Polish duchies to form the Kingdom of Poland in 1320.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The political succession to the Kraków seat in this period is documented in Polish chronicles, but the precise territorial extent of the duchy's control versus that of adjacent Piast principalities is difficult to demarcate with precision.
